verses.text: Later, when King Xerxes' anger had calmed down, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been ordered against her.
Then the king's personal servants said, "Let a search be made for beautiful young women who have never married, for the king.

Let the king choose officers in every province of his kingdom to bring all these beautiful young women to the women's house in the fortress city of Susa. Let them be put under the care of Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, and let them be given beauty treatments.
Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen instead of Vashti." The king liked this advice, and he did it.
Now there was a Jewish man in the fortress city of Susa named Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin.
He had been taken from Jerusalem as a prisoner along with Jeconiah king of Judah, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took them away.

Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah, also called Esther, because she had no father or mother. This young woman had a lovely figure and was beautiful. When her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.

When the king's order was announced, many young women were brought to the fortress city of Susa and put under Hegai's care. Esther was also taken to the king's palace and put under the care of Hegai, who was in charge of the women.

Esther pleased Hegai, and he was kind to her. He quickly gave her beauty treatments and special food. He gave her seven chosen servant girls from the king's palace and moved her and her servant girls to the best place in the women's house.
Esther had not told anyone who her people or her family were, because Mordecai had told her not to.
Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the women's house to find out how Esther was and what was happening to her.
Before a young woman's turn came to go to King Xerxes, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and creams for women.
When a young woman went to the king, she was given anything she wanted to take with her from the women's house to the king's palace.

She would go to the king in the evening, and in the morning she would go back to a second women's house, under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's official in charge of the king's other wives. She would not go to the king again unless he was pleased with her and called for her by name.

Esther was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle. Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter. When it was her turn to go to the king, she asked only for what Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, suggested. Everyone who saw Esther liked her.
Esther was taken to King Xerxes in his royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his rule.

The king loved Esther more than all the other women. She pleased him and won his favor more than any of the other young women. So he put the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king gave a great feast for all his officials and servants. It was Esther's feast. He announced a holiday in all the provinces and gave gifts generously, as only a king can.
When the young women were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
Esther still had not told anyone who her family or her people were, just as Mordecai had told her. She kept obeying Mordecai just as she had when he was raising her.
In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's officials who guarded the door, Bigthan and Teresh, became angry and planned to kill King Xerxes.
Mordecai found out about the plan and told Queen Esther. Esther told the king, and she said that Mordecai had found it out.
The report was checked and found to be true, so the two officials were hanged on a pole. All this was written down in the book of records in front of the king.
